Repo: /opt/nxeon-v2, branch design/v2 — a from-scratch visual redesign ("Nexion") of the real Nxeon hosting platform, running sandboxed (NXEON_SANDBOX=1: real DB and code paths, no VM ever provisions, no card ever charges). Read /opt/nxeon-v2/CLAUDE.md FIRST for the operating rules (never build in /opt/nxeon, never pkill -f by pattern, verification-by-screenshot discipline, etc). Login: customer@nxeon.local / wGPZqhCbsLdz (see /root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt) for most pages; admin@nxeon.local / iCwEt7PDdo0ne3YM (also in /root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt) owns some already-provisioned ("RUNNING" status) servers worth checking too, since the customer account's own servers are mostly stuck mid-provisioning in this sandbox. Base URL https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud.

CONTEXT — a long session just finished building a light theme for this whole dashboard (dark was the only mode before; light is new, toggled via `data-theme="light"` on `<html>`, tokens as `--color-*` CSS custom properties in app/globals.css) and found/fixed a long tail of bugs, including a full rebuild of the VPS server panel's "Resources" tab. You are ONE of 4 parallel agents auditing the REMAINING, not-yet-checked areas for the same classes of bugs. COORDINATION: you may rebuild (./rebuild.sh) and restart the nxeon-v2-web service as needed for your own verification — just don't leave it down when you finish, and do NOT create git commits (the orchestrating session commits everyone's work together). Stay within your assigned areas/files (listed below) so you don't collide with the other 3 agents working the same tree concurrently.

YOUR AREAS: the individual VPS server management panel's OTHER tabs — go to /dashboard/servers/<id> for a real server (query the sandbox DB directly if useful: `PGPASSWORD=e9964f4b101682befbe0deca6bf5b9e057181fec0b2245fa psql -h localhost -U nxeon_v2 -d nxeon_v2 -c "select id, hostname, status from \"Server\" where status='RUNNING';"` — db-primary.nxeon.cloud and web-prod-01.nxeon.cloud are both real RUNNING servers you can use) and click through EVERY tab except Resources/Settings, which were already redone this session: **Overview, Console, Files, Services, Backups, Networking, Activity**. The components live under components/customer/vpspanel/v2/ (VpsOverviewPanel.tsx, VpsResourceMonitor.tsx, VpsNetworkingPanel.tsx, VpsServicesPanel.tsx, VpsCredentialsCard.tsx, VpsAccessPanel.tsx, CopyLine.tsx, and others — grep for each tab's actual component from VpsPanelShell.tsx). ALSO check the game-server equivalent panel (components/customer/gamepanel/v2/*, reached via a game server's Manage link — GameHero.tsx's hero was already fixed this session, but its own tabs/sub-panels were not) and the free-Minecraft dashboard at /dashboard/free-minecraft.

THE BUG TAXONOMY TO CHECK FOR ON EVERY TAB (all of these have been found and fixed repeatedly elsewhere this session — you're checking whether the same mistakes exist in your assigned areas):
1. A literal hardcoded color (hex or rgba, e.g. `bg-[rgba(10,22,48,.5)]`, `text-[#7f9ad0]`) used for something that should adapt between themes, instead of the theme's own `--color-*` tokens / `text-tx`, `text-tx-dim`, `text-tx-faint`, `border-rim-hi`, `bg-well`, `bg-surface`, `.card`/`.card-glass`, etc. (grep app/globals.css for the full token list). On the light page these often render as either invisible-on-invisible or a jarring leftover dark box.
2. A hero/banner section with its own fixed dark background + `text-white` heading — if not wrapped in `.nx-dark-island` (also in app/globals.css), light mode's generic fix flips `text-white` to dark ink, invisible against a scrim that stayed dark on purpose.
3. `bg-white` (bare, not `bg-white/NN`) used to mean "always paint this literally white" (e.g. a toggle switch knob) — breaks because `--color-white` now means "ink" in light mode. Fix: literal `bg-[#fff]` if it must always be bright, or a proper light-aware treatment.
4. An `Icon` component (components/nx/Icon.tsx) rendered with no `tone` prop inside a colored/gradient badge that has an intended contrasting text color on the wrapper — the icon overrides it with its own default tone. Fix: `tone="inherit"`.
5. `text-white/NN` (opacity-modified) sitting on something that is NOT actually a light-mode-adapted surface — gets wrongly retargeted by the global opacity-decoupling rule meant for the page background.
6. Any canvas/backdrop using `globalCompositeOperation = "lighter"` or `mix-blend-screen`/`mix-blend-lighten` — washes to grey on light. Wire into components/nx/auroraTheme.ts's helpers (see components/nx/DomainsAurora.tsx for the pattern) rather than reinventing.
7. A `.card-on`-style selected state rendering as a solid dark block regardless of theme.
8. Genuine FUNCTIONAL bugs — broken layout, dead buttons, modals that don't close, text cut off, terminal/console rendering issues, a monitor chart that doesn't update, file browser rows that misalign, credential fields that don't copy. Note and fix anything real, not just color bugs. The Console tab in particular is a live terminal (probably xterm.js) — check it actually renders and is legible in both themes, since a terminal traditionally assumes a dark background and may need its OWN theme handling distinct from the page chrome around it.

WORKFLOW: for each tab, log in via a Playwright script (must live under /opt/nxeon-v2/scripts/ per CLAUDE.md, e.g. scripts/_audit_d.mjs — delete it when done, this repo's convention is not to leave one-off scripts lying around), screenshot in BOTH dark (default) and light mode (`localStorage.setItem('nx-theme','light'); document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme','light')` before navigating), actually LOOK at the screenshots (read them back as images), diagnose using the taxonomy above, fix in source, rebuild, re-screenshot to confirm, move on. Run `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit` after every batch of edits.

Don't invent problems that aren't there — some tabs may already be fine. Only fix what's actually visibly or functionally broken. Write a final report listing every bug found (short description + file) and every fix made, plus anything already correct.

content.content: 1 # Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork 2 3 **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with 4 a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The 5 code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but 6 `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. 7 8 Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the 9 direction and the history of what has been built. 10 11 --- 12 13 ## Where you are, and what that changes 14 15 This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is 16 meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: 17 18 ```bash 19 hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. 20 ``` 21 22 **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: 23 24 ```bash 25 npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build 26 ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. 27 ``` 28 29 **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also 30 runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, 31 terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A 32 `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, 33 then: 34 35 ```bash 36 scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 37 ``` 38 39 It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) 40 and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. 41 42 **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on 43 node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not 44 deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's 45 commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. 46 47 ## The tree 48 49 | | | 50 |---|---| 51 | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | 52 | Branch | `design/v2` | 53 | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | 54 | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | 55 | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | 56 | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | 57 | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | 58 59 `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and 60 it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` 61 builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. 62 63 Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node 64 and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing 65 to the other. 66 67 ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here 68 69 node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because 70 three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept 71 attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the 72 production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox 73 seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. 74 75 Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two 76 levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: 77 78 ```bash 79 scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title 80 scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments 81 scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ 82 scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # read-only query against PROD 83 scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else 84 ``` 85 86 **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production 87 database and the mail server. Treat it as read-only.** Never write to the prod 88 DB (the `db` subcommand refuses obvious writes, which is a guard against a slip, 89 not a security boundary), never edit `/opt/nxeon`, never build there, never 90 restart a prod service. If you genuinely need to change something on node-1, 91 **stop and ask the owner first.** 92 93 ## Rules that are not negotiable 94 95 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs 96 or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real 97 upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had 98 hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not 99 reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a 100 `0` that reads as a real measurement. 101 2. **Never run builds in `/opt/nxeon`.** That is live production; clobbering its 102 `.next` has taken the admin panel down before. 103 3. **Never `pkill -f` by pattern on either box.** `pkill -f "next start"` 104 restarted live production once. ## 4bdddc46-3b80-45ec-bc37-523e74d4fda6
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_f

#!/bin/bash
# Rebuild and restart the v2 sandbox.
#
# The tree runs a PRODUCTION build (`npm start`), not the dev server: ~0.8 GB
# instead of ~4.5 GB, on a box whose spare memory is measured against fifteen
# customer VMs. The cost is that nothing hot-reloads — every change needs this.
#
# WHY IT STOPS THE SERVER FIRST. `next build` writes into `.next`, which the
# running server is reading from. Building underneath a live server replaces the
# manifests it has open and every route starts returning 500 — this has already
# happened once in this tree. Stop, build, start. Never build in place.
set -euo pipefail

cd /opt/nxeon-v2
LOG=/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log

# ── one build at a time ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two concurrent runs write the same `.next` and corrupt it — the exact failure
# this script exists to prevent, arrived at from a different direction. It was
# survivable only by accident: the build runs inside a transient scope, and
# systemd refuses a second scope of the same name, so run two and the LOSER
# fails loudly. Relying on that is relying on a side effect of a name. This
# takes a real lock and says plainly what happened.
exec 9>/tmp/nxeon-v2-rebuild.lock
if ! flock -n 9; then
  echo "==> another rebuild is already running (holding /tmp/nxeon-v2-rebuild.lock)."
  echo "    Wait for it to finish — starting a second one would corrupt .next."
  exit 1
fi

# ── skip the marketing site ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The redesign does not touch marketing, but it is ~137 of the ~195 route files
# and most of the 254 static pages, so it dominates a build we now run by hand
# after every change.
#
# Next excludes any folder whose name starts with `_` from routing, so renaming
# the route group is all it takes. This is a SANDBOX-ONLY, TEMPORARY rename: the
# trap puts it back whatever happens — including a failed build or a Ctrl-C — so
# git never sees it and nothing different is ever merged to prod.
#
# Set NX_FULL=1 to build the whole site (do this before any staging/prod pass,
# where marketing MUST be built and exercised).
MK="app/(marketing)"
MK_OFF="app/_marketing_skipped"
restore() { [ -d "$MK_OFF" ] && mv "$MK_OFF" "$MK"; }
trap restore EXIT INT TERM

if [ "${NX_FULL:-0}" != "1" ] && [ -d "$MK" ]; then
  echo "==> skipping the marketing site (NX_FULL=1 to include it)"
  mv "$MK" "$MK_OFF"
fi

echo "==> stopping the server (it reads .next; building under it breaks it)"
systemctl stop nxeon-v2-web

echo "==> building"
start=$(date +%s)
# Capped so a runaway build is killed rather than squeezing the customer VMs,
# and niced so it always yields to them.
if systemd-run --scope --quiet --unit=v2-rebuild \
     -p MemoryMax=6G -p MemorySwapMax=2G -p CPUWeight=30 \
     bash -c 'cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && export NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 && set -a && . ./.env && set +a && npm run build' \
     > "$LOG" 2>&1; then
  echo "==> built in $(( $(date +%s) - start ))s"
else
  echo "!!! BUILD FAILED — the server is NOT being restarted on a broken build."
  echo "    Last 20 lines of $LOG:"
  tail -20 "$LOG"
  exit 1
fi

echo "==> starting"
systemctl start nxeon-v2-web
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 20 http://127.0.0.1:3021/login || true)
  [ "$code" = "200" ] && { echo "==> up: /login $code"; exit 0; }
  sleep 2
done
echo "!!! server did not come up — check: journalctl -u nxeon-v2-web -n 40"
exit 1

input.title: Fix TS build error blocking shared nxeon-v2-web
input.tldr: While auditing VPS/game panel tabs, the shared nxeon-v2-web build failed and the service has been down (502) for several minutes, blocking all 4 concurrent agents' verification. The break is in app/api/hosting/thumb/route.ts, outside my assigned scope, so I left it alone rather than risk colliding with whoever is mid-edit there.
input.prompt:
The shared nxeon-v2-web sandbox service (systemctl unit nxeon-v2-web, /opt/nxeon-v2) is currently down. `./rebuild.sh` failed with:

app/api/hosting/thumb/route.ts:100:56 — Type error: Type 'Buffer<ArrayBufferLike>' is not assignable to type 'Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>'. Types of property 'buffer' are incompatible: Type 'ArrayBufferLike' is not assignable to type 'ArrayBuffer' (SharedArrayBuffer is missing resizable/resize/detached/transfer/transferToFixedLength).

Because rebuild.sh refuses to restart the server on a failed build (by design — it never runs a broken build in place), the site has been stuck returning 502 since the failed build, blocking every agent currently working in this tree.

The offending lines are around app/api/hosting/thumb/route.ts:100 and :105:
  data: new Uint8Array(check.bytes),
where `check.bytes` is a Node `Buffer`. `new Uint8Array(buffer)` on a Buffer type-checks as `ArrayBufferLike` (which includes SharedArrayBuffer) under the current TS/@types/node combination, but Prisma's Bytes field wants `Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer>`.

Likely fix: replace `new Uint8Array(check.bytes)` with `Uint8Array.from(check.bytes)` in both spots (line ~100 and ~105) — `Uint8Array.from` always allocates a fresh, non-shared ArrayBuffer-backed Uint8Array, which should satisfy the stricter type without changing runtime behavior. Verify with `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit`, then `./rebuild.sh` to bring the shared service back up for everyone.

Please check who owns this file/change first (it may be mid-edit by another concurrent session) before editing, to avoid clobbering in-progress work — but this is currently blocking the whole shared sandbox, so it's worth prioritizing.

content.text:
## Final Report — VPS/Game Panel Tab Audit (Agent D)

**Scope covered:** VPS panel tabs (Overview, Console, Files, Services, Backups, Networking, Activity — Resources/Settings excluded per assignment), the full game-server panel (Overview, Console, Files, Mods & Plugins, Backups, Players, Schedules, Build with AI, Settings, Activity), and the free-Minecraft dashboard. Verified with Playwright screenshots in both themes wherever the sandbox allowed, backed by full source review of every component in these trees.

### Bugs found and fixed (15 files)

**Hardcoded `text-[#7f9ad0]` instead of `text-tx-dim`** (taxonomy's own canonical example) — inactive sub-nav/segment icons stayed frozen at the dark-mode blue instead of following the light-mode token, going out of sync with their own label text next to them:
- `components/customer/vpspanel/v2/ui.tsx` (SubNav — VPS Backups/Networking/Activity/Settings rail) — **verified** via Services tab screenshot
- `components/customer/vpspanel/v2/kit.tsx` (Segmented — Overview's SSH/SFTP toggle)
- `components/customer/gamepanel/v2/GameSettingsShell.tsx` (Settings rail)
- `components/customer/freemc/FreeMcDashboard.tsx` (tab bar)

**Hardcoded hover background not covered by any light-mode rule** — `hover:bg-[rgba(8,18,44,.7)]` on `components/customer/vpspanel/v2/CopyLine.tsx` painted a jarring near-black box on hover over an otherwise light card. Changed to the token `hover:bg-hover`.

**Fixed-dark terminal/preview surfaces not wrapped in `.nx-dark-island`**, so their text (`text-white`, `text-tx-dim`) silently inverted under the page's light-mode ink-flip while the black backdrop stayed black — genuine dark-on-dark bugs:
- `components/customer/gamepanel/GameConsole.tsx` (the live game console) — **verified live**, this was a real, visible break, confirmed fixed via screenshot
- `components/customer/gamepanel/v2/GameOverviewPanel.tsx` (Overview's console-peek `<pre>`) — **verified**
- `components/customer/Console.tsx` (VPS VNC viewport) — same pattern, unverifiable live (see caveat below)
- `components/customer/freemc/FreeMcDashboard.tsx`'s local `Console` (also switched translucent `bg-black/40` → opaque `bg-[#05060f]`, since translucent black was blending into the parent's now-light card)
- `components/customer/freemc/v2/FreeMcHero.tsx` (dashboard identity header) — same as the already-fixed VpsHero/GameHero, but this one hadn't been done yet

**Same pattern on colorful banners/modals** (custom rgba gradients, `text-white/NN`) — **verified**:
- `components/customer/gamepanel/v2/GameBackupsPanel.tsx` (Backups summary banner)
- `components/customer/gamepanel/v2/ModsPanel.tsx` (Mods & Plugins banner, **verified**; and the "Install anyway" confirm modal, not verified live but identical pattern)

**Bare `bg-white` toggle-switch knobs** (taxonomy item #3, verbatim) — the knob must always render literally white, but `--color-white` now means "ink" in light mode, so these were going dark. Fixed to `bg-[#fff]`, **verified via screenshot** on BackupSchedule:
- `components/customer/BackupSchedule.tsx`, `components/customer/GameAutoUpdate.tsx`, `components/customer/GameSettings.tsx`, `components/customer/gamepanel/GamePublicListing.tsx`

### Verification limits in this sandbox
- **VPS Console** never renders its real body — every server's `vmid` is NULL (no VM ever provisions), so it's permanently stuck on the "Console unavailable" fallback. Fixed by source-level pattern-matching only.
- **Free-Minecraft dashboard** is unreachable — no server anywhere has `isFree=true`, so `/dashboard/free-minecraft` only ever shows the create-form. `FreeMcHero`/`FreeMcDashboard` fixes are source-verified only.

### Checked and already correct (no changes)
VpsHero/GameHero (already dark-island'd), VpsNetworkingPanel, VpsAccessPanel, VpsCredentialsCard, ActivityTimeline, all VPS Services sub-panels (Websites/Databases/Apps/Cron), FileBrowser, GamePlayersHub/Players/Inventory/Roles, GameWorlds, GameCommandLibrary, GameBuildAI, GameSchedules, GameTierInfo, and all free-mc sub-components (GameModeSelector, GameTypeGrid, PublicListingCard, ModsTab, RolesTab, SavedWorldsPanel, ItemIcon's Minecraft-material swatches). One reverted over-eager fix: `GameActivityPanel`'s `text-[#c4a6ff]` "Running" ink is a low-but-comparable contrast to an already-shipped accent (`#7fb0ff`) I confirmed renders fine — left alone.

### Notable side-quest
The shared `nxeon-v2-web` service went down repeatedly from **other agents'** concurrent, unrelated build breaks (`app/api/hosting/thumb/route.ts`, a DB-manager type, plus a stray duplicated `_marketing_skipped` directory from a rebuild race) — none touched by me. I cleaned up the stray directory, flagged one blocking break via a background task (self-resolved before action was needed), and never edited any file outside my assignment. Service is confirmed up and rebuilt with all my changes as of now.
